note: Book 3, step 4: the teacher's top 64 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as in teacher-qwen36-capitals.json) at the scored positions, learned by KL over the top K + other (train-text with the pairs' "teacher" field, filled by tools/teacher_topk.py from llama-server on the CPU), against the same pairs learned by cross-entropy on the one next ID. Three sets, full FFN, 100 steps: A, the teacher's own replies for the 8 trained + 14 replay prefectures (hard-label run in cpu-prefecture-capitals-teacher.json); B, the hand-written frame for the same 22, the teacher scoring the city's tokens (hard-label run in cpu-prefecture-capitals-replay.json); C, the hand-written frame for all 39 prefectures outside the 8 held out (examples/prefecture-capitals-train-39.jsonl, hard and top-K runs here, lr 1e-6 and 3e-6). Compared with the untrained student on examples/prefecture-capitals-split-replay.json; in C every group but the held-out ones is trained. The teacher agrees with the text at all 201 positions (its rank 0 is the next ID) and is sharp: median top-1 probability 0.997, mean entropy 0.07 nats, only 7 positions below 0.9. Result 1: soft labels change nothing here. In each pair of runs the top-K run is within one prefecture of the hard-label run in every group, with the same README KL (top-K/hard: A 0.013/0.013, B 0.006/0.007, C 0.004/0.005 and 0.012/0.014) and the same shortcut count. Result 2: with every other prefecture in the data (C), the top FFN learns the mapping it is shown without collapsing: at lr 3e-6 the 3 different-name prefectures already right stay 3/3, the 14 same-name guards 14/14 free, the trained 8 forced 8/8 and free 6/8, paraphrases 8/8 forced, KL 0.012-0.014. So the layer-23 inputs separate the prefectures well enough to hold a lookup; the collapse of the earlier runs came from data with only the trained answers, not from the layer. Result 3: still no held-out capital is learned (0-1 of 8); they answer with the shortcut (埼玉市, 山梨市, 三重市, 愛媛市) or another prefecture's city. Free answers are cut at 16 tokens.
